items.heading: The Games
items.summary: Editorial on the special appeal of the Olympic Games and good wishes for a strong Belgrave presence in Atlanta.
items.text:
The Games

The Olympic Games. No matter how commercialised they become, or "over the top" with sports that would have been beyond de Coubertain's comprehension, the Games, when each Olympiad rolls around, bring something special to the world of athletics. Apart from the sporting feast beamed into our homes for a couple of weeks, real competition without a pacemaker in sight, there is the exciting prelude for fan and athlete alike - the need to qualify. Impressing selectors, achieving the qualifying standard and fulfilling requirements at the trials are dramas in their own right. The World Championships might be the athletic event for the connoisseur but as far as Joe Public is concerned the Olympic Games are what really count and therefore the urge for athletes to shine at this event is even greater.

Luck and good health allowing, we hope for a strong Belgrave presence in Atlanta's Olympic Stadium in a whole range of events. Our distance runners will have the problem of 34°C temperatures and humidity of well over 90% to face but the sprinters and hurdlers will enjoy the Mondo track which is already acknowledged as being "lightning fast". We won't tempt fate at this stage by naming those likely to gain selection but we wish them all the very best of luck.

items.heading: Gymnasium project completed ...
items.summary: Editorial welcoming the completion of the club's gymnasium at the Hall and appealing for more volunteer officials and team managers.
items.text:
Gymnasium project completed ...

Have you been up to the Hall recently and seen the gymnasium. There is probably not another athletic club in the country that has its own gym equipped to such a standard. Several new members have already come our way, attracted specifically by the chance to use the facilities for a mere £25 a year (£15 second-claim), and we wholeheartedly thank those who have kept this particular project on track. To have our own gym has been an aim that we have pursued for the last couple of years and it is good to see the plan draw to a successful conclusion. But this is just one of diverse schemes that we are following. Not everyone sees each project of being of equal in importance and some undertakings do not even gain immediate benefit for our club, being aimed more at assisting the community as a whole with the hope of a dividend being returned to Belgrave Harriers only in the longer term. One thing is sure, however, we have some very dedicated and hardworking officers. Although members of our Committee do not always see eye to eye when it comes to agreeing which road we should take next, it has been said recently that the Club has probably never been in such good shape.

Nevertheless, while we are pleased with the progress we are making, there is no doubt that we could do with a lot more help. On a summer Saturday we might have as many as four track & field teams in action across the country, not to mention walking and road running groups; and there may be a couple of teams in action the following day as well. This is a tremendous drain on our small band of dedicated and enthusiastic officials and team managers. Goodness knows what we would do without them. If you can contribute towards helping to run our Club in any way then please get in touch with the Club Secretary who will be only too pleased to point you in the right direction. We would particularly like to see parents and younger members (exams permitting) getting involved.

items.summary: Editorial asking athletes to tell team managers in advance if they cannot turn up for a match.
items.text:
Do us a favour

One thing that our athletes, particularly the younger ones, can do to make life a little easier for team managers is, "let the Manager know if you can't turn up for a match". There is nothing worse for a team manager who has spent hours and hours on the phone trying to put a team together, than sitting in the coach on the morning of the match with time ticking away while waiting for athletes who simply fail to turn up. A 'phone call the night before or first thing in the morning is all that is required. Unless you actually have a problem on your way to the meeting place, it really is inexcusable to keep everyone waiting for no purpose.

items.summary: Club news notes: the Shippens settling in Sydney, members in hospital, darts championship, new officials and Ted Moore back timekeeping.
items.text:
Sidetracks

Clive and Elizabeth Shippen have safely arrived in Sydney, Australia, and are currently living in Dee Why with son Mark. Clive has been running several times a week, mostly in Dee Why Park but sometimes on a circuit of Long Reef that takes in stretches of beautiful coastline. After one session, warming down consisted of an hour of lying on the beach enjoying the sunshine. Tough eh!
The Shippens soon met up with Ron Wyld and helped him to celebrate his 60th birthday along with other guests Dave Scott, Joy Gardener (Pete's mother), and Scott Wyld and almost before Clive's feet had touched the floor he was being inveigled into helping to coach pole vault at Homebush Stadium. Apparently Ron drives a claret Datsun Bluebird with yellow number plates!
Clive and Elizabeth pass on their regards to all.

Several Belgravians have been in hospital for one thing or another recently. Colin Pearson underwent gall bladder surgery just a couple of weeks ago while Keith Harris, a regular behind the tea bar on washing up duties is in nearby Atkinson Morley Hospital at the time of writing. Arthur Penstone who does so much to keep our Headquarters up to scratch has also been undergoing treatment. Our best wishes to you all and we look forward to hearing of continued good progress.

George Piddington is now more mobile and has enjoyed being visited by various members. He is taken to his local track every Tuesday by his Havant AC colleagues where he helps with coaching.

The 32nd holding of the Darts Championship for the "Denmark Pot" took place at Belgrave Hall on December 2nd and once again Bill Couzens was the victor. That makes it three years on the trot for Bill - a feat he last attained 1963-65.

We are very pleased to welcome several new officials to our ranks. A series of training courses were held at Belgrave Hall during the winter followed by tests and the result was that we now have three newly qualified track judges in Pam Davies, Leslie Earle and Richard Hearn, and two new time keepers in Terry Earle and Phil Mason. Already these good people have lent a hand at our matches and we are more than grateful for their help.

At one point during the Surrey County Championships we noted that on the Track Judges' Stand we had three Belgravians in action while across the other side of the straight three more were holding stop watches. With one or two out on the field as well, and several carrying out administrative tasks we can start to feel pleased that we are contributing a little more to our sport as a Club rather than leave it to a few individuals. But we need so many more (see our Editorial page).

Talking of Timekeepers, it's great to see Ted Moore back in action and looking remarkably well after his stroke. Ted has been timing at several school's matches and has even been up to Battersea a couple of times for our home fixtures. You can't keep a good man down for long.

items.heading: From The Belgravian
items.summary: Column reprinting items from 25 years ago (June 1971: Southern cross country, RWA 10 miles walk, Carl Lawton, Surrey League) and 50 years ago (June 1946: post-war cross-country season).
items.text:
FROM THE BELGRAVIAN

25 Years Ago ... June 1971

BELGRAVE bounced back into form in the Parliament Hill mud this February, with a highly encouraging second place in the Southern Cross Country Championships.
The most heartwarming sight of the afternoon for Belgrave supporters was that of the flying figure of Gerry North, who made a thrilling attempt to recapture his title, and had he not been hit by his old enemy 'stitch' might well have done so. As it was, his 4th place just 20 seconds behind the winner gave us a magnificent start and with another three men in the first 34 it was a good day for the Bels.
Result: 4, Gerry North; 30, Tony Brien; 32, Lionel Mann; 34, John Bicourt; 42, John Thresher; 79, Tony Fairclough. Team: 1, Reading 137pts; 2, Belgrave 221pts; 3, Hillingdon 225pts.

RWA NATIONAL 10 MILES WALK. In one of the closest races yet Belgrave only clinched the team title in the closing stages. There was never more than a few points in it as our boys battled for the vital places. Wilf Wesch, our reigning champion, was concentrating on staying safely in the race, and avoiding any possible trouble finished a comfortable fifth.
Result: 5, Wilf Wesch; 13, Carl Lawton; 16, Allan Callow; 29, Ray Middleton. Team: 1, Belgrave 53pts; 2, Lancashire W 65pts; 3, Southend 68pts.

CARL LAWTON walked brilliantly in the National 20km and clearly deserved his first selection to represent GB in a race abroad - competing over 20 kilos in Bucharest.

TONY BINDA, Peter Carton and Bill Curtin yet again filled the first three places in the final Surrey League. With Mark Clancy (5th) and Paddy Breslin (7th) Belgrave were runaway winners of both match and League title.

and, 50 Years Ago ... June 1946

THE FIRST post-war Winter season was a memorable one for the Belgrave Harriers. Our cross-country runners won every open championship. In November we had the first two teams home in the South of Thames "Junior," and the first three individuals. This in itself was a remarkable feat as all of our pre-war "cracks" cannot run this race owing to the barring clauses. In the New Year we won the Surrey County Title, whilst our Middlesex members, running for Cadogan A.C., took the Middlesex title. This was not regarded as very extraordinary as it had been done on various occasions before the war. The South of Thames "Senior" Race resulted in another win for us. Here again, a large number of our best men are "barred." The Southern Counties Cross-Country Championship, 7 ½ miles instead of the usual 10, was held from Belgrave Hall. Our Captain, Tom Carter, gained a well-earned and popular victory. With David Main third and four others in the first 20 positions, we gained a 99 points' margin over the second team. In fact our team of 12 was home before any other team had finished its six scoring men! Then to the much awaited English Championship, of which we were the proud holders. On March 9th our lads travelled to Leamington Spa and had another battle royal with our famous Midland rivals, Birchfield Harriers. Our team finished in the first 24 positions, and after a breath-taking adding up of the scores we were acclaimed winners with a ten-points' margin. We are indeed truly the Champion Club.
Of individuals, Tom Carter deserves our thanks and praise for the successful training and nursing of his team, also, of course, for his own brilliant running. It was a cause for general regret that Tom did not get another International vest. Tom had had a cold the week before the race, which no doubt left its effect. Len Herbert, by finishing seventh, was awarded an England vest, and we congratulate Len on adding his name to the distinguished company of Belgravians so honoured in the past.

items.text:
BELGRAVE DINNER DANCE

NEXT NOVEMBER - Saturday, 16th, to be precise - sees what newspaper journalists call "the end of an era." That is the date of this year's Belgrave dinner-dance (put the date in your diaries and start saving for it now) and, after thirteen years of organising it, Bill Couzens is taking a rest. He is handing this great event over to Ron Severn who will actually, with Bill's help and guidance, be responsible for this year.

Some of you may not know Ron. He joined Belgrave in 1983 after leaving High Wycombe, where he had been successively Secretary, Chairman and Trustee of Wycombe Phoenix Harriers, as well as organiser for years of the famous "Furniture Five" road race. Soon after joining Belgrave he became Hon. Treasurer, which job he did for five years, and upon giving it up he was elected a Life Member of the Club. He has been away from the innermost affairs of the "Bels" for a while, but is back now, not only for the dinner-dance, but also as a new auditor of the Club, taking over from Ray Conway, another long servant.

Ron says: "Following Bill with the dinner-dance will be almost impossible, he has made such a huge success of it for so long. All that I can say is that I plan no changes in the venue (Preston Cross Hotel) or the format, so I hope everyone can look forward to the same wonderful evening they have always enjoyed. But I need all the help I can get in the sale of tickets, so will everyone please make a special effort this year to buy them, not only to save me many sleepless nights, but also - and this is much more important - to see that Bill and his wife Gwen (who has herself made a great contribution to each year) get a grand 'send-off' and 'thank you'. "

OUR EXTENSIVE list of Club Records in the previous issue proved to be of great interest and we are grateful to those who were able to fill in some of the missing details or took the trouble to let us know of any inaccuracies. Many thanks in particular to Peter Matthews, Jacinta Moore, Steve Williams, Dave Sharpe, Charlie Dickinson, Helen Maskrey, Gary Staines and Derek Jones.

We promised to reprint the younger age group Walking Records once we had more information but quite frankly, our lads and lasses are turning in record performances with such rapidity that they are moving from week to week. We will reprint them and what we hope to do for all events in all disciplines and age-groups is produce a check-list of records broken on a regular basis.

Apologies to Rachael Parrot, whose first name we had spelled incorrectly. Incidentally, all her best walking times were believed to have been set on the track.

It seems that all of Ian Gilley's U13B Records were set in South Africa and we have no knowledge whatsoever of the conditions, venues, timekeeping standards, etc. As a result we are relegating his performances to other notable performances status and have to carry out more investigation to find out what the best confirmed performances really are for this age-group. More news in the next issue.

Michael Nicholls' correct age for under 17 records has been confirmed and we now have the correct spelling of Ian McDermott.

We are informed that 1.5k walking events are no longer held so they will also be recorded as other notable performances.

Charlie Gillett's M40 100m was patently wind assisted so it's back to the drawing board for that event although we suspect that Snowy Brooks' 12.0 from 1985 will probably stand up as the best on record.

We missed Jacinta Moore's sprint times from '95 and including them now, we note that she holds every flat running record for W35 from 100m to 5000m.

We recorded Jim Estall's '95 London Marathon as our best M40 time but had missed Charlie Dickinson's 1989 effort which was a little faster. British Athletics League (1968-1995)
Belgrave's All-Time Top 50

IT'S FOUR YEARS since we last published one of Leo Coy's lists of our All-Time Top 50 BAL points scorers. In spite of Rugby League commitments Abi Ekoku has managed to squeeze in another seven appearances for our first team and moves comfortably ahead of fellow discus thrower Ken Onuaguluchi for the first time. We have heard that Abi plans a full scale return to athletics before too long. Only one other Belgravian has racked up more appearances - Captain Phil Goedluck. 1996 should see him move into second spot. Derrick Williams' and Stu' Paton's scores are standing up well but the middle of the table has been turned over as those still regularly making the team continue to score heavily, led by Leith Marar who has come from nowhere to no. 13. Not surprisingly Neil Owen and Kassa Tadesse have also made great inroads in a short space of time while down at the bottom we have bid farewell to some old favourites including Guy Sagar and John Bicourt.

items.heading: Marathon Dave faces his toughest challenge
items.summary: Dave McMillan, who had run all 15 London Marathons, was badly injured when hit by a car on a training run and vows to run again.
items.text:
Marathon Dave faces his toughest challenge

JUST UNDER a year ago Fleet Street journalist Dave McMillan, a member of Belgrave Harriers for the last 34 years, was delighted to receive a commemorative medal and tee-shirt from the London Marathon organisers congratulating him upon being one of only 41 runners who had completed all 15 London Marathons. Dave's first athletic events had been the sprints back in the '60s but he was always ready to have a go at anything and was regularly to be seen in his teenage years, plugging away at the back of the "Southern" and "National" cross-country fields.

He was so proud to receive that letter from Alan Storey because gradually, over the years, he had got faster and faster in 10ks, half and full marathons until at the age of 47 he had just set his latest pb over the London course with 3:03:05. Club-mates jokingly reckoned that by the time he was 60 he would be down to about 2:30! Dave was determined to carry on until he was the only person left who had completed every single 'London' but sadly fate does not always favour the nice guy.

While out for a Sunday morning 13 miler in the Warwickshire country lanes near his home earlier this year and with just a mile or so to go before that hot shower, he was cruelly struck by a speeding car and received the most horrific injuries. With a leg shattered in four places, broken ribs, punctured lungs, a crushed arm ... his proud record of consecutive marathon runs was quite obviously over.

But you know, runners are such a positive breed and no-one could be more determined than 'Dave Mac'. For a start he was pleased to be alive. The ambulance rushing him to the Radcliffe Infirmary in Oxford had to radio ahead to report that he was likely to be dead on arrival unless special surgery was carried out immediately. Another ambulance with the necessary equipment was dispatched and at a rendezvous in an Oxfordshire country lane an innovative emergency operation was carried out.

A three month minimum predicted stay in hospital was then reduced to a month as Dave oh! so painfully carried out every exercise and more prescribed by the doctors. He had already told the hospital staff that he would be running again and they devised additional 'work-outs' to keep tendons and muscles in tone for that big day in the future.

Incredibly, only two months later, he is already getting about in his wheelchair although the jarring caused by cracks in the pavements has him gritting his teeth and he has had to return to hospital for a bone graft. Once more he has vowed that he will run again and who can possibly doubt it.

items.heading: Safeguarding young athletes and coaches
items.summary: Past President Reg Hopkins relays a BAF message on protecting young athletes and coaches from abuse and false accusation, and takes on the role of club contact, with his photo.
items.text:
Safeguarding young athletes and coaches

"THE DISCUSSION between BAF, Sports Council and other sports concerning statutory and recommended procedures for protecting young sports persons against abuse, and those working with them against malicious accusations of misbehaviour or abuse, continue. It is becoming increasingly apparent that the key agency in putting these safeguards into effect can only be the athlete's club. For it is here where young athletes and adults interact in an athletic context. Protocols are going to have to be established by which clubs vet appointees to positions in which they work with the young, and then monitor them in doing so. References and affidavits may be needed and sub-committees and confidential files safely and securely kept. Will your club be able to cope?"

At a recent meeting of the Club's Management Committee the Secretary brought the above message from BAF to our notice. It was agreed by all present that we should give it our full attention. Having had to deal with this subject, in which I have received considerable training as part of my full time occupation as Youth and Community Officer, I readily offered to act for the Club in this matter. Following the request of the Committee and on the recommendation of BAF I have purchased the information pack concerned with our sport, and will consult it when and where necessary.

I feel sure that all Belgravians will understand the need to give attention to this danger that can threaten both young person and adult, and will give me their full support in what can be at times a very sensitive situation. All I need to say at this time is ... you know whose responsibility it is to act in these matters on behalf of the Club and therefore whom to contact if you have any fears.

Reg Hopkins, Past President. Telephone [phone number withheld].

items.text:
An Englishman in New York

NEW YORK CITY MARATHON
12 NOV 95

AS THE 26.2 mile charge through the streets of New York gradually drew to a conclusion and Central Park loomed ahead there were still 11 men battling it out for the top prizes. The Mexicans were out in force with Silva and the Garcias; Lopuyet, Kagwe and Koech were there from Kenya, Portuguese representatives were Matias and Pinhero and there were the South Africans Thys and Moqhali - oh! and of course the lone Briton and Belgravian Paul Evans. It was tough little German Silva making the running at 23 miles, piling on a pace that at last began to whittle down the leaders. Two miles to go and it was down to three: Silva, Evans and Koech. As the diminutive Mexican's searing pace bit harder and harder first the African fell away - and then Paul faltered, only to get back on terms again. Together they raced on until with 800 metres remaining the low geared Silva opened up just enough daylight on the Belgrave Harrier and at such a speed there was no coming back again. Exciting stuff!

items.text:
Vets in Ireland

THREE veteran Belgravians, Laurie O'Hara, Fred Paget and Charlie Dickinson flew to Ireland for the annual home international cross country races, this time held at Malahide Castle, Dublin on November 18th. Laurie was selected to run for the England M60 team while Charlie was a reserve for the England M45's. Fred went in an advisory capacity!

It was indeed a splendid weekend. The hospitality was superb, the course beautifully cut green grassland in front of the magnificent castle, and the weather cold but with clear air and brilliant sunshine.

The standard of running, particularly in the men's race, was awesome with Nigel Gates getting the better of Ireland's Jerry Kiernan and SLH's Barry Attwell. Laurie had to settle for silver in the M60s behind Scotland's Hugh Rankin and collected another silver in the team event. His time over the 9km course was 30:50.

Charlie Dickinson came 4th in the Open Veterans race held over the same circuit in 27:50, a time that would have got him a team medal in the international race - but he did easily win the competition for drinking the most Guinness!

Another Record Haul from President Snowy Brooks

BEING PRESIDENT of Belgrave Harriers doesn't seem to have slowed Super-Vet Snowy Brooks down at all. After last year's foray to the World Championships he had previously decided to take 1996 a little more easy but somehow the performances just seem to keep on coming. February 18th saw him at the Southern Counties VAC event at Crystal Palace where he clocked 8.3 for 60m and 9.7 for the 60m hurdles - but this was just a warm-up. At the British Veterans Pentathlon Championship at Birmingham Arena on March 2nd he led from the first event to the last, coming home over 700 points ahead of the second M50 with performances of 60mH/9.60, LJ/5.58, SP/11.90, HJ/1.51 and 1000m/3:50.86. Both the high jump and long jump were M50 Club Records and his final score of 3647pts was just 50pts shy of his best ever M50 pentathlon mark.

YACHT '3'
WIMBLEDON, 7 OCT 95

"Hmph! Mystic Meg stands more chance of getting the handicaps right than you do ..."

Every year Charlie Manning's ritual abuse of the Hon. Handicapper gets more inventive but never one to hold a grudge, Arthur Bruce this year gave him enough leeway to keep him off the back of the pack for a change. Entries were up for the second year in a row even if there was a Veterans' race over at Petersham and at last the field began to look like a race again. Even young Laurie was out scorching the SW19 roads again, sending the memories of onlookers drifting back over the years to races of days gone by.

At the other end of the age-scale, nine years-old Paul Graham was having a great day. A jog in the morning at Battersea with Snowy and Daley Thompson loosened him up nicely for this three-miler and his determined sprinting down the finish stretch earned him the admiration of all. Pete Gilbey and Laurie O'Hara were so taken with the young man's efforts that they spontaneously awarded him their sports voucher prizes - at which Paul responded by offering them a go of his "power-ranger".

But it was Misery Manning who had the last word when watching our President haul his decathlete's frame over the last yards:

"What ... I thought he was supposed to be an athlete ..."

items.text:
Hard pressed at home !

REEBOK SURREY CC, LEAGUE DIVISION 1 RACE 1
WIMBLEDON, 14 OCT 95

Our officials were hard pressed on this day. As Don Anderson was running round the course laying out the trail of flags and tape he was unaware that mischievous youths were were busily adjusting his markings. With many of our Saturday afternoon runners happily ignoring the race as they ran past on their way to the Park, we were already short of pointsmen and as a result the youngsters' race was neatly diverted across a golfing green and off towards the horizon. After a long detour they approached the finish from completely the wrong direction. It didn't affect the result of the race as all except one lad followed the same route but it did affect the golf tournament which was called off ! Irate golfers had to be placated. When this was followed by a letter of complaint from one of the participating clubs with the suggestions that we should have people with radios at intervals around the course - we should have pointsmen stationed within sight of each other at every turn - that we should have a senior runner at the head of the field leading the way (any runner capable of doing that would currently be among our our scoring ten!) - well, it make's one wonder if there isn't a better way to spend a Saturday afternoon.

In spite of all this, Amir Becirhodzic had great pleasure in getting home 2nd, and with fellow Bels Kevin Quinn, Steve Beaver and Peter MacDonald packing in close behind, Boro' of Hounslow only just pipped us for the Under 17 team win. Our mighty midgets the under 13s also gave us second place even though they had run way over the correct distance.

While all this was going on senior Belgravians were still arriving at the start - some new faces - and some old - including Stu Paton and John Gladwin. No fewer than 29 claret and gold vests were among the initial charge as the starter sent around two hundred-odd runners on their way.

Herne Hill's Taylor made the race his own from the very beginning although he never got right away. His clubmate Jon Solly was in close attendance after the first circuit with Aldershot's Jackson and Hare & Hounds' Oxborough strung out behind. Our second-claimer Adrian Passey led the Belgrave contingent but although we were strong in numbers, for most it was the first run of the winter season - and didn't it show. Far from gaining a good start in the series we found ourselves shunted right back to 7th place when the points were tallied. Even newly promoted Ranelagh got ahead of us.

One man who was highly delighted was Stuart Paton. He sailed into the scoring ten to prove that there is plenty of life in his legs yet. New members Ray Foley and Nick Kello closed in our team.

SURREY COUNTY VETERANS CC CHAMPS.
PETERSHAM, 7 OCT 95

Only a few years ago this event was perhaps one of the most popular races for Belgravians with as many as thirty veterans taking part. This year it was down to a bare dozen runners with complete teams only from the ladies and M40's.

The reasons are simple. Firstly, the date has moved progressively forward from its traditional spot at the end of October and this year clashed

Surrey Vets continued . . .

with Belgrave's own Yacht handicap. Secondly, for the last two years the course has been held over the very tough lower circuit which includes climbing the dreadful Petersham hill three times. Many who ran it last year opted out this year, and some who did it this year will never do it again (ask Doug Maughan).

Belgrave ladies fielded the same team as last year but Jacinta Moore never felt happy and was well down from last year's fifth place. Nina Mills finished 6th W45 and Hilary Saw was only a minute and a half behind her. They placed 8th as a team.

Again, John Mather was down from last year when he had a blinding run, but won the battle with Don Anderson to finish first Belgrave runner in 21st place. It was good to see the improving and very keen Tony Binda next, followed by Paul Roche. Chris Taplin had a good run in 49th and the M40 team finished 7th.

John Wasbrough and Tony Stone renewed their M50 battle of last year. This time it was John who was just ahead at the finish. With Pat Newell injured and Arthur Bruce lining people up at Wimbledon for the 'Yacht' it was only Bert Stroud who ran in the M60's finishing 7th.

items.summary: Team manager Alan Mead's review of the men's 1995-96 road and cross country season, culminating in the London Marathon team win.
items.text:
Harriers once more

We didn't expect our Men's Road and Cross Country team to set the world alight during the winter just past but nevertheless, things have begun to bubble nicely and looking back, the general feeling is one of satisfaction. A corner on the road to greater things has been turned and we have a clearer view of what we can do.

In the Surrey League we came steadily from behind to end up at Coulsdon with our best team place in several years. We were well supported by Gary Staines but just as pleasing was the confidence beginning to creep into the team with half our scorers getting used to finishing in the 20s. What we must do next season is start off stronger - get a couple of low key events under our belts before the winter season begins in earnest - and then we can definitely aim for a final team place in the top half of the league.

The South of Thames 'Junior' race at Crowthorne saw us in the medals while the 'Senior' event where we only belatedly entered a team gave us the individual winner. Both of these races could provide rich pickings for us next year. Few of our runners currently suffer from the barring clauses that prevail in these races - so let's go out next winter and get barred in a big way!

We never did have the main championship events inked into our calendars but when one looks back one can see that with a little better organisation we could have won the Surrey title and with Matt Yates finishing in the 60s in the National one couldn't help getting excited about what we could achieve if we had enough runners with the same aim.

By the time the relays came around things were looking better and better. Tackling the ECCU 4x5k cross-country event for the first time was an eye-opener. We had a hot team but those Northerners were hotter still. Who would've thought that clubs would turn out their top men two weeks in a row; 14k of cross-country at Newark followed by another 5k at Mansfield. We might have missed out on our dream of winning national medals in that four stage event but at least we featured again among the names of the traditional cross-country clubs - Bingley, Coventry, Border, Tipton, Belgrave ... with others like Birchfield in our wake.

Then came our own road relay promotion where we swept the board. The Belgrave 6-Stage is beginning to look as if it might remain a regular event and it all adds to the pride and confidence that we need when it comes to showing that we are indeed still a harrier club as well as an outstanding track and field outfit.

On to the Southern 12-Stage. Things got so exciting during the fortnight beforehand that our aim of a top ten spot got forgotten as we changed our target to top six and then saw ourselves as potential medallists. Sadly the wheels came off during the last few days but to end up 8th was a fine achievement and surely a herald of what is to come.

Finally the London Marathon gave us the high profile win that we were looking for. Of course we had a brilliant start with 3rd and 9th from Paul Evans and Gary Staines but there had been prolonged negotiations between our management team and Nike, the BAF, the SEAA and the Race Referee, simply to ensure that out top two men would be eligible to score for us due to the fact that they were contracted by Nike to wear their Elite vest while in the team race club colours "should be worn". Our negotiations bore fruit and as a result we may well be pressing for an amendment to BAF's rules to make them more workable in today's sport.

So now it's all before us. If we really do want to move on, we can. We have a good team running the show and as Team Manager I would like to thank Charlie Dickinson, Gordon Biscoe and Don Anderson for their help but most of all thanks to you the runners led by Captain 'Gerry' Adams and Vice-Captain Roger Alsop. Already I am looking forward to the prospect of next winter's campaign. There's the challenge of completing teams in the major championships, County and National 6-Stage Relays to have a crack at, the defence of what we have won this winter past.

Alan Mead

items.summary: Report and results of the Priory 6x2½ mile cross country relay at Reigate Priory on 4 Nov 1995, where captain 'Gerry' Adams helped Belgrave to 6th.
items.text:
A 'stormer' from the Captain

PRIORY 6x2½m CC RELAY
REIGATE PRIORY, 4 NOV 95

Our best showing in recent years was in 1991 when a Gary Staines last leg of 12:19 took the Bels to 6th. No superstars this time out so our final position of 6th after half a dozen circuits of Priory Park has got to be considered highly satisfactory.

Roger Alsop gave us a solid start by coming in 7th with Tonbridge making the running thanks to the day's fastest leg from Skelton. The young team from Kent held on to their lead on leg two with the first of the Graffin twins swinging into action but the field had closed up drastically behind with our own 'Gerry' Adams running a stormer to take the Bels up to 3rd. We should have been able to analyse our Captain's run over and over again at leisure but unfortunately Colin Pearson forgot to set the record button on his camcorder!

Boxhill snuck past a fit looking Rob Turner and Bruce Barton, suffering from the sniffles held onto 4th as the last legs approached but Windsor were getting ominously close. Sure enough the Berkshire club's McHarg had the measure of Belgrave's Said Chettati and then Phil Carstairs had the pleasure of setting out for the final stage with Brighton's Andy Bristow breathing down his neck.

Pick of the 'B' runners was City Dealer Nick Kello who'd have gone faster still had he arrived a little earlier and taken the 1st stage.

Fastest in our women's team was Laura Wilson, still not quite 16 years of age and seemingly able to tackle any distance from 200m to 3k.

items.heading: We're in the medals
items.summary: Report and results of the South of Thames Junior cross country at Crowhurst on 11 Nov 1995, where Belgrave were second team and captain Graham Adams 4th (the season review on page 9 places this race at Crowthorne).
items.text:
SOUTH OF THAMES "JUNIOR" CROWHURST, 11 NOV 95

We're in the medals

It was heartwarming for all those involved in cross country to watch a fine second place from our team and an inspired individual 4th from captain Graham Adams.

Overnight rain, the first for several weeks, had softened the woodland paths which together with some very tough hills and more rain during the race made for a demanding course. A narrow downhill start produced the predictable manic rush with the Graffin twins from Tonbridge already heading the fray just ahead of Graham Adams. Then came a bunch of Belgravians, Roger Alsop, Nick Kello, Phil Carstairs, and Said Chettati nicely packed in the low twenties.

The end of first short lap saw Graham maintaining his position in the leading bunch, Roger moving up, Nick dropping back slightly, and the others roughly the same. Futher back Steve Willimont looked unhappy but Tony Binda and Paul Cooper were running well.

At the halfway stage a breakaway group of seven runners were forcing the pace with Graham Adams hanging on at the back. Roger Alsop continued to move up into the low teens and Phil Carstairs, not too well lately, was beginning to look uncomfortable. Graham made a huge effort after the long hill on the final lap picking off three tired bodies in a long run for home. An excellent effort.

Roger showed that he is fast getting fit again after achilles tendon problems and a disappointing track season. He too finished strongly and got up to 11th. Next came Said who had got past Phil Carstairs and ran himself almost to a standstill in finishing 29th, another very good performance.

Although suffering badly, Phil managed to hang on to the end without dropping too many places which was a good job as Belgrave only finished one point ahead of Basingstoke. Further down the field Nick Kello pulled a calf muscle but battled on gamely and cheerfully to the end. Tony Binda did well to finish 94th and we all know he has the potential to become a very good veteran. Paul Cooper too has a great deal of natural ability, he just needs to train harder and drink less!

In all a very good day, well done Belgrave and well done Graham.

items.heading: League hopes take a dive
items.summary: Report and results of the second Surrey Cross Country League Division 1 match of 1995-96 at Richmond Park, where Belgrave's seniors were 7th but moved up the league, and the young athletes' teams placed second and third.
items.text:
League hopes take a dive

REEBOK SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 1 RACE 2
RICHMOND PARK, 18 NOV 95

High hopes and hard work in attempting to round up a strong team counted for nothing. While we went through the list of Belgravians we had hoped to put on the starting line but who had failed to appear for one reason or another, Hounslow were at their strongest and romped to a clear win with 8 men finishing in 28. The Bels who were there all ran well, greatly improving on their first race positions but we simply had to go back too far to close in the team.

Luckily for us, but unluckily for the "Irrepressibles," South London H crashed so badly that they dropped from 6th after match 1 to 8th here and as a result we actually moved up in the league!

Jim Estall's 22nd came just the day before the Epsom '10' - there's no stopping this man when he's on song - and after two races he had put himself well in line for the vets title.

A very warm welcome went to new member Dave Beaver, one time second placer in the National Junior Cross Country Champs for Polytechnic H. Dave's been around the club for a season or so while son Steve has been making a niche for himself in our under 15 team, and finally he took the plunge and signed the dotted line along with other son Chris. Dave then celebrated by going straight into the scoring ten even though far from fit.

Before you read through the results, we must point out that Charlie Manning's "dnf" was not due to that gentleman's inability to complete the course - it was simply due to the fact that he was a little worried about keeping the timekeepers hanging about and a lot more worried about getting his car out of Richmond Park due to the gates being closed at dusk!

Among the youngsters, great running came from Amir Becirhodzic who raced through strongly for 3rd with the rest of the team queuing up for points just behind. As a result second team place went the way of our under17s/under15s while the under 13s also scored well headed by David Bates, Chris Beaver and that mighty nine year-old, Paul Graham. At the halfway point in the league both these teams were lying in 2nd spot.

items.heading: Sweeney on his tod in 'Surrey'
items.summary: Report on the Surrey County Cross Country Championships at Frimley, won by second-claim Belgravian Chris Sweeney on his return from three years of injuries, with Graham Adams 7th and Steve Beaver 6th in the Under 15 Boys.
items.text:
Sweeney on his tod in 'Surrey'

SURREY COUNTY CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS
FRIMLEY, 9 DEC 95

Those who braved the icy conditions at Frimley were treated to a wonderful victory by Chris Sweeney, returning to competition after three years of injuries. Chris was running as a second claim member for Belgrave and was unfortunately unable to score for the team (not because second-claimers are barred but because he only entered at the last minute). The rest of the squad all ran well but just lacked sufficient depth to claim any medals although it is worth noting that had Chris stated his intentions earlier we would have been within a point or two of winning.

Two times around the frozen playing fields and both Chris Sweeney and Graham Adams were well up in the leading pack; Chris looking very relaxed, Graham already working hard. Further back Jim Estall and Roger Alsop were nicely placed in the second group. Then the field climbed up the steep bank into the woods for three tough undulating circuits.

By this time the sun had disappeared and with it any semblence of warmth. Many runners never really warmed up and found the hard rutty conditions very tiring. After the first lap Chris Sweeney had already forged a useful lead and he looked comfortable and confident as he floated over the ground with his economical style. As the race progressed so his lead grew, all the way to the finish. This was really the first indication of the form which later took Chris to a successful Grand Prix series and a Great Britain vest in the World Cross Country Championships.

Graham Adams again led by example and battled around the course to finish in 7th, an excellent result which reflected his strong early winter form. Then Jim Estall, unhappy with the cold, but finishing a fine 14th, again ahead of BVAF National Champion Barry Atwell and also Bob Treadwell. Roger Alsop ran steadily for 27th, then a gap before Mike Nouch and Junior Galley in the late fifties. One more engine room runner here would have given the Belgrave team medals even without Chris Sweeney, but it was not to be and it was thanks to Tony Stone for completing the scoring six back in 185th position.

Leo Coy's lads looked as if they would be on for a set of medals in the Under 17 Men's group but unfortunately Simon Alexander suffered an asthma attack, putting paid to those hopes. Highest placed first-claim Belgravian of the day was Steve Beaver whose 6th place in the Under 15 Boys race must be ranked as his finest run to date.

items.text:
Darren 2nd at Norfolk

At Caldecott Hall, Norfolk, Darren Mead ran into controversy when recording the same time as the winner in the Norfolk CC Championship. Turning out for his second-claim club as one is perfectly entitled to in County CC Champs., Darren found himself accosted by a Norfolk official who told him that he would not be allowed to run. After a heated discussion (not the best preparation for a race) it was agreed that the official was wrong and that he could indeed represent Thetford. But the day had more twists in store yet. Tucked in behind the leader as the finish was neared, Darren unleashed a sprint for the line and although our man felt he got his nose in front, as did his rival and various other onlookers, the decision went against him and second place in the same time as the winner was all he could claim. We believe that this is the first Norfolk CC title Darren has ever lost.

Conditions were so slippery that most had trouble keeping their feet at some stage but Marcello seemed to suffer the most, looking as if he'd be much happier wearing a pair of skis. Phil Carstairs yo-yo'd up and down the top ten as the race progressed, gaining places on the rolling grassland and hills but losing them again every time the murderous descent was tackled when less cautious souls let the brakes off and dodged the rocks and trees like fell runners. Foxy old Charlie Dickinson worked his way through gradually while lightly built Dave Beaver just could not believe how well he was going.

items.text:
Staines leads league revival

REEBOK SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 1 RACE 3
WIMBLEDON COMMON, 6 JAN 96

We know the Common well but there are some areas rarely visited by our runners - and for good reasons. Whether the area now known as the "Butts" really was used for military purposes in the 18th and 19th century is unknown (the area around the Windmill certainly was) but anyway, this series of muddy clay banks hemmed in by thick bushes makes for decidedly unfriendly running conditions - although Thames Hare & Hounds seem to delight in taking their courses right across them.

We were pleased to see Gary Staines turning out. He felt a little below par but was soon locked in battle with training partner Jon Solly as they toured the first circuit. Jim Estall, Roger Alsop, Bruce Barton and Phil Carstairs were well forward, and showing that if you've got class it soon makes itself evident, Dave Beaver was not far behind. Limping along prior to coming out at half way, Nick Kello had badly twisted an ankle, putting paid to his running activities for a few weeks.

Into the second half of the race and Gary applied the pressure on the hills. It was too much for Herne Hill's Solly and as the leaders swept down along the edge of the playing fields the crowd waiting at the finish could see that the Belgrave man had levered open a comfortable 50 metre gap.

We missed our Captain and his customary place just inside the top ten (he was away in Sweden for a few days) so next Belgravian was Jim Estall, doing his bid for the veteran title no harm at all by crossing the line in 18th. The rest of the team had mostly preserved their places. Charlie Dickinson found the jarring conditions tough for 45 year-old bones but nevertheless had the beating of Alex Luce; Steve Hewes was out for the first time but not eligible to score, so it was left to Mikes Webb and Nouch to close in our team in the 80's. At 5th the team result was better but we still had plenty of room for improvement.

James Venning added his weight to the under 17 team and with our regulars in action again it was another 2nd place with 3rd for the under 13s led home again by David Bates.

It's deceptively hard, is Brockwell Park. Parkland it might be but there is hardly a level stretch to be found anywhere. items.text:
Our best men's league result in years

REEBOK SURREY CC LEAGUE DIVISION 1 RACE 4
COULSDON, 17 FEB 96

Belgrave's senior men finished 4th on the day in the last Surrey league match of the season, their best result in years and at last some real encouragement for the team and reward for the huge effort put in by Alan Mead over the winter.

There was already a confident atmosphere before the race with most of the recognised Belgrave distance runners reporting for their numbers. Then Gary Staines strolled up with Linda. This was Gary's second consecutive League race, only a week after his victory in the South of Thames "Senior," a really unexpected bonus for the team. One could immediately sense the positive effect this had on everyone else.

And now we are really beginning to get an engine room. Not just the old reliables, Graham Adams, Jim Estall, Roger Alsop and Phil Carstairs, but add to that list Bruce Barton, the new revelation Dave Beaver the much improved Alex Luce, and don't forget new second claim member Steve Hewes who will hopefully be scoring for us next season. Yes, there is already an air of excitment about next season.

As the runners climbed the long haul up to the downs for the first time, Gary looked very comfortable sitting in the first group. Then the already mentioned Belgrave vests stretched from the early twenties to the fifties with Junior Galley looking relaxed after his Caribbean holiday (perhaps a bit too relaxed) and Said Chettati, struggling hard against the effects of his fast for Ramadin. Then there was the reliable Mike Nouch, Pete Gilbey and Marlon Anderson.

By the time they reached the steep hill after two miles Gary was controlling the race from the front with Dave Taylor of Herne Hill, not long out of hospital, struggling to keep in contact. Graham Adams, Jim Estall and Roger Alsop were all packing together in the early twenties with Bruce Barton running a sensible race a few places further back, followed by Phil Carstairs, dropping slightly, Dave Beaver and Alex Luce.

The pattern continued at the front until the last quarter of the race when Gary sped away from a very tired looking Taylor to win with ease by a margin of nearly half a minute. Next for Belgrave up the steep hill the second time was Jim Estall, but only just ahead of Graham Adams and Roger Alsop. It was the determination and 1500m speed of Graham that enabled him to lead the trio at the finish. For Jim, this final flourish gave him the individual veterans' title for the whole series.

Only just behind was Bruce Barton in 30th, ever improving in his first real season on the country, a very good run on a tough course. Next Belgravian was Steve Hewes showing the benefit of those ten mile training runs with Roger Alsop and company but he was only just ahead of Dave Beaver, Phil Carstairs and Alex Luce, all finishing in the mid fifties.

Poor Said had to stop to be sick on the second lap subsequently losing next scoring place to Mike Nouch. To make things worse he then lost out to his 3000m adversary Junior Galley who closed in 93rd.

This result moved Belgrave up to 6th overall in the league well away from relegation danger and hopefully providing a platform on which to build for next season. We really need to strengthen the middle order so that the final scorers are in the fifties, not eighties and nineties, plus we need the the occasional guest appearances by some of our stars: Darren Mead, Matt Yates, Chris Sweeney and a fit again Kassa. We shouldn't always have to rely on Gary. Yes, it could be a good season next winter!

But while the seniors were congratulating themselves on at last showing signs of a revival, the youngsters were also pleased with their performances. Another battling performance from Amir took him to 4th place and individual Under 17 winner for the 1995/96 series. Kevin Quinn and Peter McDonald were next in but one to watch in the next couple of seasons is Steve Beaver - an Under 15 but chasing the other three home. Steve Beaver was first Under 15 on the day and yet another individual winner for Belgrave in his age group.

Our Under 13 team was again headed by David Bates and Paul Graham and if these lads and their team-mates can continue to apply themselves in future seasons the way they have this winter, then the Bels will have some fine runners moving up through the ranks.

items.heading: Matt Yates wins the "Parker Bowl"
items.summary: Report and results of the National Cross Country Championships at Newark, where 1500m runner Matt Yates was 66th, Belgrave completed no team and Janine Brown gave the club its best female 'National' performance.
items.text:
Matt Yates wins the "Parker Bowl"

REEBOK NATIONAL CC CHAMPS
NEWARK, 9 MAR 96

The Belgrave men's team is always full of surprises. At a time when 14k of cross country seems unpopular among our members, 1500m star Matt Yates fancied having a run and, donning a brand new pair of spikes and a Belgrave vest to tackle the Showground and farmland of Newark, proceeded to give us our best individual position since .. well, you tell us. The official results also showed the name of K.Tadesse (Bel) at 50th but all we can say is that it wasn't our Kassa or anyone else we knew running under his number - a shame, because 50th and 66th would have given us a good start for the team race - if we'd had a couple more men prepared to give it a go.

Bingley were phenomenal. In a field of approaching 2,000 finishers they had six scoring men home in 32 with two others inside 100. Tipton's team were also all placed inside the first 50 but maybe we'd give them all something to think about the following week at the relays.

In fact we failed to complete a team in any category. Our Under 17 Men came closest and would have placed 21st but for the fact that the "Vest Police" disqualified Peter McDonald for failing to wear a Belgrave singlet. The fact that at that time with our stocks run down we simply did not have one to fit him cuts no ice with folk like the "VPs" and one can only hope that such actions don't put the young man off the sport.

Janine Brown, running in the youngest girls' age group gave us our best ever performance in female "National" cross country races and we'll be watching this talented athlete's progress with great interest in the years to come.

items.heading: Bels. fifth in National C.C. Relay
items.summary: Report and result of the English National Cross Country Relay Championships at Berry Hill, Mansfield, where Belgrave's team of Graham Adams, Matt Yates, Darren Mead and Gary Staines finished 5th on the club's debut in the event.
items.text:
Bels. fifth in National C.C. Relay

ENGLISH NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY RELAY CHAMPS.
BERRY HILL, MANSFIELD, 16 MAR 96

We felt that we needed a high profile win to give the team a boost and looking at the fixture card this National 4 x 5k Relay seemed to be the one where we could do the business. For a start we "only" needed four class runners and secondly, it was the week after the National Cross Country Champs. when all the opposition would be "knackered" while we had been resting up. When organiser Dave Denton acknowledged the entry he couldn't help adding the note: "Potentially the winning team, Alan - if you can get them all out!"

Well, we had a darn good try, but it wasn't to be. For one thing, we'd failed to grasp that clubs like Bingley and Tipton and Border have enough top class runners to turn out week after week. Secondly, in a race of only four legs, however good your top men are, they simply run out of race track when trying to make up ground over a mere 5k.

In damp and freezing conditions 'Gerry' Adams got us under way and while the announcer gave us plenty of air-time due to his pleasure at seeing the Bels making their debut in this Northern dominated event. 'Gerry' found himself running his heart out in an attempt to give us a good start but was actually on the receiving end of some startling running and was disappointed to complete his leg 17th of the 73 starters. He looked a bit dispirited but generally, with the hills and soft going, the times seemed to be getting on for a minute slower than a genuine track 5k and he would have been pleased with a 14:42 on the all-weather oval. In the meantime Coventry Godiva had gone clear at the front with an 8 second margin over Border AC. Border's 'B' team were 3rd, Tipton 4th and we were 37 seconds in arrears.

Next up was Matt Yates and he set about the teams ahead as if it was war. He had some large gaps to bridge but nevertheless, Birchfield, Morpeth, Liverpool and Sheffield were just some of the teams that fell to his all-devouring stride and he must have been delighted at out-running Sale's Kevin McKay by ten seconds. Border had gone ahead now with a 14:58 from Russell - the day's fastest at that point - while Bingley had gone 2nd and Tipton were up to 3rd. The gap from first to our own 11th had grown by another 6 seconds.

Dave Denton hit the mike again: " ... and Belgrave are now moving through the field as Matt Yates hands over to Darren Mead ... great to see him in action again ..." Five more clubs fell by the wayside as Darren took his new Nike vest past Chelmsford, Sale, Derby ... Border were still holding on at the front and we were now 6th with Gary eager to take his turn in the chase. Those at the very front were not letting up any and we were now about 50 seconds in arrears and knew that it was too much even for Gary. But one thing was for sure - it was going to be exciting.

Amazing! What actually happened was that Gary ran faster than any man had done that afternoon - so far. Although in a period of very heavy mileage for his forthcoming London Marathon attempt, his 14:43 had him rocketing past Loughboro's Bruno Witchalls. But up ahead, Bingley's Hawkins clocked 14:40 to run down Border and take the lead, only to be chased by Coventry's Troumans who went even faster with a 14:32 to all but win on the line. Virtually all the day's fastest times were clocked on the last leg by runners in the first five and Gary was rendered powerless to make any major advances.

Looking back, we had to be pleased, and as Darren said after the event, "Next year ..."

items.heading: Gabby and Gary the fastest as Bels. scoop the prizes
items.summary: Report and results of the Belgrave-Nike Road Relays at Wimbledon (dated '23 Mar 1966' in the heading, a misprint for 1996), won by Belgrave 'A' in both the men's 6-stage and women's 3-stage races, with Gary Staines and Gabby Collison fastest.
items.text:
Gabby and Gary the fastest as Bels. scoop the prizes

BELGRAVE-NIKE ROAD RELAYS
WIMBLEDON, 23 MAR 1966

It looks as if this 6-Stage promotion for men and 3-Stage for women is likely to become a permanent feature of the fixture list as Thames Valley's race seems destined not to return. We hadn't necessarily intended holding the event again but with Nike's impending sponsorship and the need - don't faint you old timers - to have a few run-offs to assist with selection for the Southern 12-Stage, the wheels of organisation began to turn again. The lap was extended to a more acceptable 2 miles 1013 yards and in spite of the low-key advertising, 29 men's teams and 10 women's teams faced President Snowy Brooks for the start.

The initial stage gave us a three-way Belgrave clash as Dave Pamah (preparing for the track season and with no recent form) battled with Junior Galley (well into marathon training but desperate to do the 12-Stage) and the spritely Dave Beaver. Within just over 13 minutes selection problems had been eased a little as all three of our men's teams came in well up but with Dave Pamah holding the aces in spite of blowing up at 2 miles while actually in the lead. City of Portsmouth were 1st stage leaders while in the women's race Windsor had a 39 second gap over Helen Maskrey for the Belles.

Now the fun started in earnest as "Stainsey" set out on what proved to be by far the fastest lap of the day (with one exception), gaining a 43 second lead for Belgrave in the process. What a runner - and he'd already done god knows how many miles and a hill session in the morning!

Nikki Haines determinedly turned the screws on Windsor to draw up to within 4 seconds of the lead in the women's race, paving the way for a superb run from Gabby Collison whose last leg 14:19 was a full 40 seconds faster than any other female runner (and a good deal faster than many of the men).

The men's 'A' team were also not to be headed again as Bruce Barton and Jim Estall laid the ground for a blistering run from Roger Alsop and a final flourish from Kassa Tadesse. But we dropped a hint that there was another fine run to come - and on leg four, this time running for the 'C' team Gary churned out another astounding run with 11:54 to put the 'Cs' in front of the 'Bs' again, a lead they were to hold until young Kevin Quinn got the better of Leo Coy near the end.

It really was an enjoyable event with the needs of the athletes paramount in the minds of the officials. Herne Hill's Jon Solly ran three stages paired up with Hare & Hounds' Wayne Oxborough who ran two - and yet they still managed to finish 2nd (although not eligible for prizes). The prizes donated by Nike were most generous and visiting team managers clearly stated their intention to return next year, should we continue. The race looks set to run and run.

BVAF NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPS., PRINCETHORPE COLLEGE, RUGBY, 17 MAR 96

The small mainly M60 team of Belgrave runners were joined by Alastair Aitkin and Jeremy Hemming for the minibus trip up the M40 to Princethorpe College. The undulating grassland couse set in the lovely grounds of the college provided a tough test for the runners and an ideal view for spectators. With the M40 winner Nigel Gates finishing in 34:38 we had proof of the severity of the course.

Unfortunately, it was not a good day for Belgrave. Poor Laurie O'Hara had been unwell all week and should not have run. He looked rather ashen when the bus picked him up at Iver, and he had to stop to be sick half way through the race. Even so, he went past Ron Higgs again but had to be content with 11th M60.

Perhaps the best run was by Pat Newell, new to M65, who started very cautiously but worked through strongly to finish just outside the medals in 4th. Further back was Charlie Walker who kept going well to finish 10th M65 ahead of Bert Stroud and an unhappy looking Carl Cross. All that resulted in a 4th place for the M60 Belgrave team.

Rex Bale was a lonely Belgrave figure in the M50's and ran well to finish first Belgrave on the day in 43:50 for 46th place.

items.heading: Southern Comfort
items.summary: Report and results of the South of England 12-Stage Road Relay at Thurrock, where a depleted Belgrave team finished 8th of 57 and then declined its National 12-Stage place.
items.text:
Southern Comfort

SOUTH OF ENGLAND 12-STAGE ROAD RELAY
THURROCK, 31 MAR 96

As stated elsewhere, the new management crew could hardly contain their excitement over the team that was beginning to shape up in the weeks before the race and there is no doubt that had we been able to hold it together until the day we would have been right up there in the medals. But the art of team management is turning promises into reality - and we have a little way to go yet. Of our entered 24 names we soon lost Michael Kazimierski - not eligible until 1st May, Nigel Powley - similarly not yet available after switching from Colchester, Phil Carstairs - on holiday in America, Stu' Paton - last minute working, Gary Staines - urgently in need of a much longer race preceding 'London', and with the race just 48 hours away 'Gerry' Adams was unable to switch shifts at the Fire Station and Dave Pamah went down with a cold. One after the other the reserves were called upon and before we go any further we must thank them for filling in at the last minute - especially Mark Anderson who cut out his normal Saturday training run to stand by the following day at the race should anyone else fall by the wayside at the last minute.

In the face of all of this our 8th place from 57 teams must be seen as a success and if we didn't do quite as well as we might have, we can draw comfort from the fact that next year our team is sure to be that much more powerful.

We decided to start off strongly and then gradually apply the pressure in the middle, hoping that we could gain enough ground so that when the gaps built up later in the race our reserve men could hold on for a reasonable position - and that's just the way it worked out.

Handling his long stage expertly, Roger Alsop set the ball rolling nicely with his 13th place in a time that was to stand up as second only to Darren Mead's - and only by 23 seconds at that. Similarly Rob Turner was our second fastest short stage man as he gained five places for 8th.

Marcello had been suffering from a groin strain in the weeks before and had been a doubtful starter. He gamely plugged away but we were down to 14th with a quarter of the race gone. Up ahead the lead had been changing with each leg. GEC held the early advantage through Tony Whiteman, then it was Boxhill and London Irish before things began to settle down with Boxhill again leading but with Hounslow and Blackheath ominously moving closer.

Our own stage four was taken by Alex Luce; with a sore throat he was not at his best and he lost seven places before we started to wind things up again as halfway approached. While Blackheath went ahead for the first time our own Jim Estall did plenty of damage himself as he clocked our third fastest long leg and recovered five places. Now it was up to Matt Yates to impose himself on the field.

What an asset this man is. Half a minute faster than anyone else on the stage, he ripped the opposition apart to take the Bels up to 7th with a lightning 12:29; the second fastest by anyone on the day. Darren Mead was third fastest on his leg with 23:27 and now just Blackheath, Hounslow, Boxhill, Chelmsford and Aldershot remained ahead.

As we expected, the gaps were now large. We couldn't in all honesty expect to gain any more ground and it was a case of hanging in as well as we could. Bruce Barton's short stage came and went - still 6th. In spite of cramping up badly Junior Galley lost only one place as Thames Valley got by. Forty-five year-old 'toughie' Pete Gilbey set out with Shaftesbury's international John Sherban on his shoulder, had him race past within seconds, but 14 minutes later came back home with the Shaftesbury man nowhere to be seen (he'd pulled a muscle). Last minute recruit for a long stage Mike Webb enjoyed his Essex outing, giving way to Old Gaytonians and finally a Friday night recruit Nick Kello celebrated his birthday (and the Team Manager's) by holding steady in 8th.

Footnote: The top twenty teams qualified for the National 12-Stage but on the night of the race we took the decision not to take the place we had earned at Sutton Park. Several of our runners would be involved in the London Marathon and would therefore be unavailable, while others were off for warm weather training or other such activities prior to the track season. It was agreed that it was better to end the season on a relatively high note than take a team to the Nationals that would probably finish in the 40s.

items.heading: London Marathon Team Champions
items.summary: Report and results of the 1996 London Marathon, run as the club championship, in which Belgrave won the team race in 9:56:02 led by Paul Evans (3rd, 2:10:40) and Gary Staines (9th), with Stuart Paton's marathon debut.
items.text:
LONDON MARATHON
Team Champions

LONDON MARATHON
21 APR 96

This race must go down as the classiest Club Championship of all time. Paul Evans was expected to produce his usual high standard run while for Gary Staines, it was his second attempt at going all the way, humid conditions making things difficult in his first attempt in Vienna just on 12 months ago. Then there was Jim Estall - as fit as a flea - and a whole bunch of others who may well spring surprises: Marcello Bizio, Stu' Paton, Junior Galley, Mike Kazimierski ... who would close in our team on what we hoped would be a winning occasion? What no-one bargained for was the unseasonably high temperature with the mercury being pushed to 21°C (70°F) by midday and there is no doubt that it had a great effect on the way the race turned out.

Early on a large bunch including all the main players broke away with Paul Evans' blond head bobbing away in the midst. Gary's start was more conservative and by Tower Bridge he was conspicuous in the second wave of international runners with former winner Eamonn Martin already struggling just ahead.

Looking for a time in the mid 2:20s, Jim Estall had set off at 5½ minute mile pace but he soon realised that this was not going to be the day for such a pace and eased off to 5:45s for fear of blowing up. Mike Kazimierski came past him at Rotherhithe so as this pair crossed the river it was 'Kaz' ahead with Jim tucked in not too far behind. Bouncing along, Stuart Paton looked in great shape, accompanied by Marcello and an incognito Matt Yates out for a training spin. Surely no team could match this. Six men through in about 200 places.

The second half was murderous. As the leading bunch was whittled away around the Isle of Dogs Evans continued to look comfortable but Gary's pack seemed to disintigrate. For Stuart the signs of dehydration became evident. He had suffered similarly on a recent long training run so he knew he was in for a bad time. Junior and Jim were also feeling the heat but Mike Kazimierski's run was looking better and better although all of them were now running a long way down on their "hoped for" times.

Well, we all know now that among the front runners Mexico's Dionicio Ceron was the iron man. When he made his break with just over 3 miles to go it was all over for the others as he powered on to his third consecutive victory. Belgium's Vincent Rousseau looked strong along the Embankment while Paul and the young African Kabiga battled it out for third and fourth. A good number of club members had gathered here to cheer on their team and when Gary Staines hove into sight in 9th place they jubilantly proclaimed their excitement at seeing that our second man through in the Club Championship was also the next Briton. What a second half he had run and tired though he was, a wry smile briefly flickered across his face at his Embankment reception.

Now we wanted a third and fourth man through to complete the team. The gaps were huge - far greater than normal - but at last a Belgrave vest was spied ... and it was Kazimierski, some five minutes down on his projected time but running strongly and in the 50s. The trouble was, he was not eligible for team competition until 1st May. Then, drenched from tipping water over himself, Jim Estall came out of the Blackfriar's tunnel, but where now was our legitimate 4th scorer?

It was some twenty minutes before a tired Junior came through followed by the battered remnants of our team. There had been all sorts of drama around 20 miles. Stuart had completely hit the wall and walked for ages between 17 and 19 miles before Dennis Williams of H/W got him going again and it was at this stage that Junior passed him. Marcello had reached 20miles in 1:57 but then took an hour for the last six miles, his groin injury having got to him again. Our chances in the team race seemed to be blown away.

There were plenty more Bels to cheer on. Lionel Mann had an amazing run over quarter of an hour faster than last year while Paul Cooper was thrilled to bits with his effort.

Then late that night came the news that in spite of everything we had indeed won the team race. All the teams had been equally decimated by the warm conditions but our scoring quartet's times added together came to 9:56:02 and we easily had the measure of any other squad. And just think, if Mike Kazimierski had been eligible we would have been home in 9:31:15 - a team time out of this world - not to mention the fact that just after the race Anthony Robertson (125th in 2:36:34) signed up for the Bels!

One of the most interesting points had been Stuart's debut. As a class 1500m runner, his club-mates, in changing-room discussions, had him down as anything between 2:35 and 2:50, so was he disappointed with his run? Well, he'd like to have gone better and as he said, " ... with a 1500 if you run a crap race one week you can always run another one the next weekend - but there's no way I'm doing another marathon for a bit. Still, it's got to me. It's a whole new sport - and I will be having another go."

items.heading: Race Walking
items.summary: Unsigned introduction to the Race Walking section reviewing the young race walkers' successes since the event was reintroduced in winter 1994/95.
items.text:
Since Race Walking was re-introduced to the Young Athletes in the Winter of 1994/95 it has taken off like an express train. In every age group the Club is now having major successes. From Young International down to County Championships the team has proudly represented the Bels. In 1995 we won no less than twentytwo National, Regional and County Medals, six English School Vests, two South of England Vests, two County AA Vests, and already we have been informed that at least three of the team will be representing the South this year, with another two or three on the borderline for selection.

It is impossible to mention every Young Race Walker in this short piece, although they really do deserve it, so if your name has not been mentioned, please accept that everything written applies to you all.

We have travelled far and wide, and if the British League Team think they travel a long way, try this for a year's travel - London (many times), Dublin, Weymouth, Chesterfield, Birmingham (three times), Coventry, Leamington Spa, Brierly Hill, Bexley (four times), Stoke-on-Trent, plus taking part in the Thameside League.

In the 1994/95 season we finished fifth out of twentyfour teams in the RWA Younger Age Groups' Grand Prix Series, and we only competed in half the matches. This year we are expecting to improve and we are fighting for second place with Sheffield RWC and Steyning AC (two of the country's top Race Walking Clubs). The Under 15 Boys won their 1994/95 series and are expected to be in a similar position again when September comes around. The Girls, although small in number, are also improving on their previous year's position.

items.heading: Race Walking Excites The Club
items.summary: Steve Whorlow Snr., the younger age group walking team manager, reports on the young walkers' championship golds, new club records and the team's spirit.
items.text:
In February we took a near clean sweep of the Kent County AAA Road Walking Championships with five Golds (out of six), followed by four SEAA Road Walking Championships Golds in March, and with numerous Silver and Bronze medals. We have been very successful in these Championships and expect to continue on the Track this summer.

By the time you read this the event will be over, but in May the National YAG Race Walking Championships are due to be hosted by Belgrave Harriers in Folkestone and are expected to be the highlight of this Club's race walking year. As it is home ground for many, and with the fanatical family support that the team has, even more success is expected to come our way.

Club Records are beginning to fall after many years of sitting on the shelf - and not just by a few seconds. In the Girls' records Laura Fryer has knocked 2 minutes off the Club's Under 13 3000m track record and she has also taken the 2km, 2.5km and 3km records. Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith took the Under 15 2km road record in Dublin with 11:28 and Lucy Asling the Under 11 1km and 1.2km road and 1000m track records. In the Boys' Section records have gone to Nigel Whorlow in the Under 15, 17 and 20 age groups. He now holds the Under 15 2km and 2.5km road and 3000m track, the Under 17 2.5km, 3km road and 5000m track, along with our best ever times for Under 17 and Under 20 at 11km road records. Richard Banham and Stephen Whorlow are sharing most of the Under 13 records between them. All these marks, along with many others that have stood for a long time, are expected to fall during 1996. This can only be good for the future of Race Walking in the Club.

We have become known throughout the country as the best TEAM in terms of support towards each other. Every athlete without question supports every other member of their team. No disappearing after the finish, they get their breath back and cheer in those that are still coming home. Cheering those in other races is also the norm - and not just our own team, because we have made many friends throughout the country who also deserve our support. This in turn gives the Club a name for good sportsmanship. We also have a great family support being built up.

As the Younger Age Group's Walking Team Manager it has been the most exciting year I have had with the Club, and working with Carl Lawton and other Senior walkers, we should be able to make Race Walking secure in the Club for many years to come. The Club has supported the event well and we hope that our successes have made the unexpected expenditure worthwhile. It has now moved out of being a minority section of the Club and Race Walking is now on a par with the Young Athletes Track & Field and Cross Country sections within the Club.

Steve Whorlow, Snr.

items.heading: New Year's Day Walks Victoria Park, 1 Jan 96
items.summary: Report and results of Loughton AC's City New Year Walks in Victoria Park, an RWA Grand Prix event where Belgrave's young walkers finished second overall to Leicester.
items.text:
NEW YEAR'S DAY WALKS
VICTORIA PARK, 1 JAN 96

On New Year's Day 13 Young Athletes travelled to Victoria Park, London, to take part in Loughton AC's City New Year Walks which was also an RWA Grand Prix event. It was another successful day in most of the age groups. In the Under 11 Girls' race (1km) our youngsters showed us what the future has to offer - and it looks very rosy. Lucy Asling took 1st with Dannielle Johnson 2nd and Rebecca Andrews 3rd. Not surprisingly they also took the team race.

We only had one Under 13 Girls' entry but that was enough because fast improving Laura Fryer gained her first win in a RWA Grand Prix event.

In the Under 15 Boys we had similar success with Chris Stanford taking a very good 3rd but with the withdrawal of two of our walkers after only 500m it was left to the younger boys of the team to bring home the joint U15/U13 team prize. Well done Chris Stanford, Stephen Whorlow and Robert Bignall.

In the Under 17 age group we again took two of the minor prizes. An unwell Kelly-Anne decided she still wanted to race and was rewarded with 2nd in the Ladies under 17 race. Nigel Whorlow took 3rd in the Youth's event even though he walked for three-quarters of the race with a loose shoe lace. (Never agin Nigel!)

Overall the Club gained 285 hard won Grand Prix points and stood second only to Leicester - possibly the top Race Walking Club in the country.

items.text:
MOLLY BARNETT GRAND PRIX
COVENTRY, 3 MAR 96

Another long journey, to Coventry, where our youngsters again set walking alight with their enthusiasm. A quote from the Race Walking Record (April 1996) remarked on the increase of numbers and shows how they are now being accepted as a regular force in YAG Race Walking " ... and it's not all down to the Belgrave travelling show making the trip for the first time - they did have fourteen finishers, about one third of the increase ".

The races were of mixed age groups which does not always lead to good racing as the youngsters tend to go off fast with the older walkers.

In the Under 13/15 Girls' race Laura Fryer came 14th (4th under 13), losing out on 3rd by 5 seconds. Chris Stanford placed 7th in the equivalent Boys' event, having an "off" day but still recording a pb of 10:52. Richard Banham led home our Under 13 Boys with 25th.

Kelly-Anne Parker-Smith was 19th in the Women's 5km (4th U17) and to add to the team's misery of just missing out, Nigel Whorlow also came home 4th in his Under 17 Men's 10km, 15th overall.

With so many 4th places it meant that the team came home for the first time in many months without a trophy between them - leaving them even more determined to succeed at Weymouth.
